##  · DOC1-timer-rule-ids — Rule IDs for timer.md's Security properties (RED-18)

Status: **open** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 3

### Kernel-set fixer (R1 remainder) · Question

Event: `7ecfd9eeeee90a6df21dfa31a8638dfa` · 2026-09-26T07:42:39Z

> RED-18: docs/kernel/timer.md's Security properties has three sections with no rule ID (S4 says every property has one): 'Every blocking call returns by its timeout' (that is I13, owned by invariants.md), 'A passed deadline comes first' (a budget whose deadline passed is destroyed before any later kernel operation; nothing defers expiry), and 'Timer work is paid by whoever asked for it' (R12 (scheduling)'s charging, now with the whole-cost destruction rule). The checker does not enforce S4 here; only the owning page may write the defining heading. B3 fixes the servers set to start at R25.
> 
> RECOMMENDATION: no new IDs. The three sections become citations of owned IDs, headed so the checker reads them as citations, not definitions: 'I13 (every blocking call returns by its timeout), on the timer'; 'R10 (destruction) at a deadline: a passed deadline comes first'; 'R12 (scheduling) for timer work'. The deadline-first text is R10's deadline path, so budgets.md's R10 section gains one sentence stating it ('A budget whose deadline has passed is destroyed before any operation that enters the kernel after that instant').
> ALTERNATIVE: allocate R25 (deadlines first) on timer.md and shift the servers set to R26; costs a B3 change and every later server ID.
> Which do you want?

### Architect · Answer

Event: `8ba0aec2a15c1cdfe17e68106c3c67eb` · 2026-09-26T07:42:55Z

> Decision: take the RECOMMENDATION. No new IDs, and the servers set stays at R25. All three are properties already owned elsewhere, and timer.md is only where they happen. A new R25 would give one rule two homes: it would restate R10's deadline path and I13's ordering.
> 
> Headings on timer.md: "I13 (every blocking call returns by its timeout), on the timer"; "R10 (destruction) at a deadline: a passed deadline comes first"; "R12 (scheduling) for timer work". Each is a citation with timer.md's mechanism (expire_due at every kernel entry) and its test. The definitions stay on invariants.md and budgets.md.
> 
> Amendment to the R10 sentence on budgets.md: it must also carry the equal-instant order, which is part of the same rule and has a visible consequence (time.rs module doc). Text: "A budget whose deadline has passed is destroyed before any operation that enters the kernel at or after that instant: expiry runs first at every kernel entry, before anything reads the entering process. At an equal instant, timeouts expire before deadlines, so a caller whose call a server took, and whose timeout falls with the server budget's deadline, gets Timeout with its lend consumed, not Dead with it returned." The R12 citation on timer.md points to the whole-cost destruction billing agreed on DOC1-kernel-code-findings (part 3). Until the package lands, that is a stated departure there, not a property.
> 
> S4 holds: every property section on timer.md names an owned ID. The checker does not need to change, because only budgets.md and invariants.md write the defining headings.
